question: Which statement best describes Elements?
options: Tags are the angle-bracket labels around an element name. Many elements have an opening tag and a closing tag; some are void elements and do not wrap content. It is like opening and closing a box around an item. Learn the element’s syntax so nesting is correct. In practice, an anchor navigates; a button performs an action in the current interface. In a real page, a link with an href can be opened or copied using normal browser behavior.

An element marks content and its role. `

Hello

` creates a paragraph: the tags surround its text. It is like a labeled container for one kind of content. Browsers build a document tree from elements and use that structure when displaying the page. In practice, a heading names a section, while a paragraph holds related sentences. In a real page, use a heading and paragraphs to structure an article before choosing colors.

An attribute adds information to an element. An image uses `src` for its file and `alt` for a text description; a link uses `href` for its destination. It is like adding labeled fields to a container. Use only attributes that fit the element and quote their values. In practice, a form label gives its input a name that can be announced by assistive technology. In a real page, a form label names its input even when the visual layout changes.

A semantic element describes its job. A `<button>` is for an action; an `<a>` is for going somewhere. It is like choosing a tool by its purpose. Meaningful elements provide built-in keyboard and accessibility behavior that a generic styled box does not. In practice, cSS can change a semantic element’s appearance without changing its HTML meaning. In a real page, a button activates an action and includes familiar keyboard behavior.
